*[Bug 19144] New: wilcox.test(exact=TRUE) can return p-values outside [0,1] with a zero difference*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19144>

            Bug ID: 19144
           Summary: wilcox.test(exact=TRUE) can return p-values outside
                    [0,1] with a zero difference
           Product: R
           Version: R 4.6.x
          Hardware: x86_64/x64/amd64 (64-bit)
                OS: Linux-Ubuntu
            Status: UNCONFIRMED
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Accuracy
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:tasuku.kobayashi@gmail.com|tasuku.kobayashi@gmail.com>

In R 4.6.0, R 4.6.1, and current R-devel, the one-sample exact path of
wilcox.test() can return finite p-values outside [0, 1] when the sample
contains a zero difference.

I reproduced this on the official R SVN trunk revision r90451, built from
source and run under Rscript --vanilla on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu. The method
reported by R was "Wilcoxon signed rank exact test", there were no warnings,
and repeated calls were bitwise identical.

Deterministic reproducer (n = 100 integers, exactly one zero):

    x <- c(52,49,65,23,-30,67,31,79,35,7,94,75,58,50,97,-1,73,37,46,
           34,-54,78,66,70,15,76,3,82,42,5,17,51,88,12,89,22,56,64,43,
           28,25,48,-33,8,53,36,60,32,91,24,96,18,-71,-27,45,99,77,69,
           26,68,57,95,40,98,72,86,6,16,0,93,90,38,59,14,47,19,-41,84,
           92,63,39,87,9,80,10,85,20,62,13,21,83,4,11,44,81,55,2,61,
           -29,74)

    for (alt in c("two.sided", "greater", "less")) {
        p <- wilcox.test(x, exact = TRUE, alternative = alt)$p.value
        cat(alt, format(p, digits = 17), "\n")
    }

Observed on R-devel r90451 (the same displayed values were observed in
R 4.6.0 and 4.6.1):

    two.sided  -7.5495165674510645e-15
    greater    -3.7747582837255322e-15
    less        1.0000000000000038

Expected: every p-value must lie in [0, 1].

Three separately implemented exact-arithmetic lineages agreed on the
conditional zero-preserving signed-rank distribution. The exact reference
values are:

    greater =
      409667043355 / 316912650057057350374175801344
      -> correctly rounded binary64: 1.2926812586409632e-18

    two.sided =
      409667043355 / 158456325028528675187087900672
      -> correctly rounded binary64: 2.5853625172819263e-18

    less =
      158456325028528674992491941179 /
      158456325028528675187087900672
      -> correctly rounded binary64: 1.0

The signed-rank statistic is 4755 in both R and the exact computations.

Reporter-side numerical diagnostic (not an R Core root-cause
attribution): for this input, the floating mass function constructed by
.dsignrank() sums to 1.0000000000000038. The CDF used by .psignrank()
has the same value. The following identities reproduce the reported
outputs bit-for-bit:

    greater   = 1 - CDF
    less      = CDF
    two.sided = 2 * (1 - CDF)

The normalization excess is about 2920 times the exact positive upper
tail, so the complement becomes negative. Summing the floating upper
tail directly instead gives 1.2926812586409682e-18, which stays in
[0,1] but is 26 ULP from the correctly rounded exact value.

This also means that a final clamp alone is only a domain guard: for this
reproducer it would turn the negative upper tail into zero, although the
exact upper tail is strictly positive. I have not assumed a preferred
complete repair. I can prepare an SVN diff after maintainer guidance on
the intended numerical strategy.

For comparison, the same calls in my tested R 4.4.3 environment returned
in-range values through the older behavior, which removed the zero and
used the asymptotic path. In the tested versions, the out-of-domain behavior
is present from R 4.6.0 onward and is not present in R 4.4.3, which follows a
different fallback path.

R-devel identity:

    R Under development (unstable) (2026-08-27 r90451)
    Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu

*[Bug 19124] strptime() fails to parse %w of '0' in LC_CTYPE=C*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19124>

--- Comment #2 from Suharto Anggono (<mailto:suharto_anggono@yahoo.com|suharto_anggono@yahoo.com>) ---
(In reply to Michael Chirico from comment #0)
With `%U`, week 1 starts at the first Sunday. So, Sunday of week 0 doesn't
exist. In fact,

    strftime("2026-01-04", "%Y %U %w")

gives `"2026 01 0"`.

On the other hand,

    strftime("2026-01-04", "%W")

gives `"00"`.

The added code in `w_strptime_internal`, which is supposed to fix Bug 15195, is
wrong.

In the formula, `save_wday - w_offset` part is supposed to mean how many days
_ahead of_ `w_offset`.

          if(tm->tm_yday < 0) tm->tm_yday += 7;

should be

          if(save_wday - w_offset < 0) tm->tm_yday += 7;

.

Alternatively, discard it entirely, but replace

    save_wday - w_offset

in the formula with

    (save_wday - w_offset + 7) % 7

.

    strptime(paste("2026", c("00", "01"), "0"), "%Y %W %w")

should be one week apart, `2026-01-04` and `2026-01-11`.
